validation.title: Independent five-lobe perfusion validation against normal V/Q SPECT/CT

protocol.decision_rule: Both reconstruction series must satisfy every per-lobe bound, the five-lobe RMSE bound, and the right-lung aggregate bound after explicit renormalization of the published rounded fractions. No model parameter may be fitted to these validation values.

sources.citation: Bourhis D, Robin P, Essalah A, Abgral R. V/Q SPECT for the Assessment of Regional Lung Function: Generation of Normal Mean and Standard Deviation 3-D Maps. Front Med. 2020;7:143. doi:10.3389/fmed.2020.00143.
sources.measurement_method: Relative lobar 99mTc-MAA perfusion counts from V/Q SPECT/CT, reported with and without CT attenuation correction
sources.cohort: Seventy-three consecutive examinations interpreted as strictly normal by two nuclear physicians, with no low-dose CT parenchymal or pleural abnormality and pulmonary disease history excluded
sources.data_access: Aggregate lobe means transcribed from Table 1 only; subject-level datasets remain available from the authors on request
sources.cohort_independence: Independent authors, cohort, and V/Q SPECT/CT modality relative to the Lee 2022 dual-energy CT calibration source used by model v7

limitations: The source is an observational reference distribution rather than a controlled prospective validation of MEHLISSA.
The source cohort was selected from clinically referred patients whose scans and low-dose CT were normal; it is not a population-based healthy-volunteer cohort.
Both reconstruction series originate from the same 73 examinations and therefore probe reconstruction sensitivity rather than independent cohorts.
Table 1 values are aggregate means rounded in percentage units; the no-attenuation-correction entries total 100.1 percent and are preserved as published before explicit unit-sum normalization.
Supine V/Q SPECT/CT perfusion fractions do not establish validity in upright posture, disease, childhood, or subject-specific anatomy.
The engineering compatibility thresholds are based on the source's attenuation-correction sensitivity and are not statistical equivalence margins.
